title: Frozen versions: full-18 validation and test trends
main_point: Compare accuracy and cost across frozen versions without treating versions as replicates.
method_notes: Recomputed arithmetic task means from exactly 18 unique problems per model/split; no imputation.

title: R70B instance signal beyond problem and exact size
main_point: Instance-conditioned selection is compared with the same picks reassigned within exact size.
method_notes: R70B val/test, full scope; singleton dilution retained. Whiskers are empirical permutation quantiles.

title: Winner-runner margins and cost tolerance answer different questions
main_point: Small winner margins do not imply that a wrong selected solver is inexpensive.
method_notes: R70B test margin counts; task-normalized regret shares. Tolerance curves use complete 18-task equal means.

title: R70B errors: winner rank and named-family cost budgets
main_point: A frequent rank-2 error can contribute less total regret than a rarer rank >3 error.
method_notes: Frozen R70B test; native winner rank; additive regret contributions retain the full task denominator. Optional family summaries use complete equal-task means.

title: Winner frequencies versus solver picks on TSP and CVRP
main_point: Compare concentration and under/over-selection without mistaking marginal frequency for instance signal.
method_notes: Per-dataset test frequencies; all models must agree on native winner frequencies and pool identities.

title: Frozen models agree on predictions and share error sets
main_point: Prediction diversity and shared wrong-instance sets are distinct diagnostics.
method_notes: 11-version matrix subset where available; complete 18-problem pairs only, equal task weights. Optional cohort vote/union are ALL18-only; hindsight union is not an accuracy ceiling or selector.

title: Changes from R45A: corrected, harmed, and net regret
main_point: Accuracy gains and losses need not have symmetric cost consequences.
method_notes: Paired frozen predictions against R45A on each task test split; sign of regret retained; exported bootstrap ranges.

title: Four datasets: native Top1 and winner coverage in Top3
main_point: Compare available frozen methods separately on TSP test, CVRP test, TSPLIB, and CVRPLIB.
method_notes: Native Top1 and native winner Top3 coverage; local NSS only; missing cells excluded without substitution.

title: Four datasets: selected cost relative to the instance oracle
main_point: Compare available frozen methods separately on TSP test, CVRP test, TSPLIB, and CVRPLIB.
method_notes: Raw dataset-native selected/oracle means; annotation uses ratio of means, not average relative regret.

title: Score confidence, empirical correctness, and cost of wrong picks
main_point: A high score need not imply either frequent correctness or a cheap error.
method_notes: Test TSP/CVRP/ATSP only, no macro. Ten score bins, minimum n=10 and wrong n=5; wrong costs use cached FP64 costs/native winners.

title: Train-fixed Top3 portfolios versus adaptive R70B coverage
main_point: High shortlist coverage can come from a train-fixed set, while single-pick regret remains a different objective.
method_notes: Train-selected k=3 fixed portfolios, held-out test evaluation; adaptive best-of-3 actual cost included when exported. Native Top1/Top3 remain distinct; single-pick cost has a different execution budget.

title: Training histories and validation-only checkpoint diagnostics
main_point: Validation CE, winner accuracy, and cost can prefer different epochs within a frozen run.
method_notes: Complete task-macro histories, local stage epochs; selected_epoch is independent of retrospective validation_selection_sensitivity optima.

title: Cost scale and solver rarity explain different parts of the error budget
main_point: Large-scale instances can dominate absolute excess cost; rare winners can still have unique cost value.
method_notes: Within-task evaluation cost quartiles; no fitted policy. Solver contribution measures oracle cost increase if that solver were removed; native frequency can include ties.

title: Train-defined advantage regions: held-out transfer
main_point: Compare train region behavior with validation and test without refitting regions on holdouts.
method_notes: Explicit region_id/split metrics; top eight by train n, no holdout ranking; no mixed-task aggregate.

title: Score-conditioned decisions recover a little; added features are mixed
main_point: Coarse score-conditioned mean-gap decisions recover a small part of R70 loss; added descriptor gains do not agree across metrics/splits.
method_notes: Historical holdouts exploratory; still below R45A reference; no claim of absent residual information; point axes are zoomed.

title: Concrete solver preferences transfer across observed instance regions
main_point: Preferences can reverse with observed size/demand and recur on held-out instances.
method_notes: No holdout threshold selection; no causal attribution to the features; exact rules and supports in regions/regions.csv.
